summary: Format conversion of the pinned Dealign CYBERSECURITY NVFP4 checkpoint. Weight-faithful to that checkpoint; no base-model tensors substituted.

architecture.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Dealign CYBERSECURITY)
architecture.type: Mixture-of-experts transformer with linear-attention layers, n-gram per-layer embeddings (PLE) and a multi-token-prediction head

source.derivation: Experts requantized from NVFP4 to searched Q2_0; n-gram table FP8 x scalar to IQ4_NL; dense trunk, MTP and vision from the checkpoint's own BF16 tensors

quantization.label: Searched Q2_0
quantization.experts: Q2_0, per-block scale search (2.25 bits per weight)
quantization.vision: F32 values of the BF16 source, narrowed to BF16 exactly

main.content: part 1 of a two-part split GGUF: the conversion's main GGUF with split keys added (scripts/backends/repack_split_gguf.py; tensor payloads and metadata verified identical)

ple.content: part 2: the per-layer n-gram embedding (PLE) table, IQ4_NL, streamed from disk row by row; byte-identical to the conversion's standalone PLE GGUF

vision.source: Cyber's own projector (its BF16 source values in F32, which Splash narrows to BF16 exactly)

memory.note: Splash's own plan for this model (/status): target weights plus the DFlash2 draft (0.49 GiB), INT8 KV at 131072 tokens, prefill/decode/state/pipeline/runtime reserves, BF16 vision. BF16 trunk as the authoritative source stores it, run exactly through BF16 and BF16S planes (patch 0002). Measured peak wired 48.37 GiB (whole machine, backend A/B 2026-11-13).

evidence.speed and memory: backend A/B on Splash-m1 1.6.1-m1-ds1, 2026-11-13 (short, 8K and 32K prompts, repeated prefix; temperature 0; Manifests/evidence/backend-ab)
